A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SGR research. All 17 pages of v2 and 18 pages of v3, including appendices, support comparison. Visual inspection resolved figure extraction issues, and relocated tables and examples could be matched.

before.justification: V2 reports original SGR benchmark evaluations, stage ablations, step-length sensitivity results, and token-cost analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds L2M comparisons, SimpleQA and DROP evaluations, and a human preference study.

M1.justification: The two-stage guidance-and-answer procedure, paragraph delimiter, minimum step length, duplicate resampling, and accumulated-answer context remain unchanged. Appendix A.1 retains identical prompts. The new Self-Reflection subsection explains the existing procedure without introducing a component.

E1.justification: V3 adds actual evaluations on SimpleQA factual questions and DROP paragraph-based reasoning questions in Section 4. This extends coverage beyond the retained mathematical competitions and MMLU-STEM to distinct factual and reading-comprehension tasks.

E2.justification: V3 adds Least-to-Most prompting to the retained benchmark comparisons for Qwen2-7B, Qwen2-72B, and LLaMA3.1-8B (Tables 1, 5, and 6). The new QA comparison also includes Qwen3-8B-Instruct, Claude-3-Sonnet, and GPT-3.5. Earlier comparators remain present, including those moved into the appendix.

E3.justification: Section 5 introduces a distinct evaluation protocol: 20 sampled MATH questions, 10 mathematics annotators, and blinded independent pairwise preferences using correctness, clarity, rigor, completeness, and explanation quality. Existing benchmark splits, decoding settings, precision choices, and iteration limits remain unchanged. New QA split and metric details are not clearly specified.

E4.justification: V3 adds a supplementary human assessment of reasoning-answer quality against QwQ and SBP. The existing stage ablations, 100–600 step-length sweep, step-count analysis, token-cost comparison, and train-station case study are retained; their relocation does not constitute new analyses.

E5.justification: V3 newly asserts statistical significance for the human preference advantage over SBP in Section 5, but supplies no named test, statistic, p-value, or confidence interval. Averaging results over top_p values 0.7 and 1.0 remains unchanged; no additional seed or repeated-run procedure is documented.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial result entries for L2M and the new evaluations. Table 4 reports SGR DROP scores of 70.7 and 75.6 for Qwen2-7B and 72B; Figure 5 reports SGR preferences of 61.0% against SBP and 38.5% against QwQ. Retained benchmark and ablation scores match. The DeepSeek-Llama improvement annotation changes from +12.3 to +8.0 in v2 Table 3 versus v3 Table 2.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces substantive formal theory or proofs. The operational step specification remains unchanged, and v3's Self-Reflection discussion adds conceptual explanation rather than mathematical definitions or derivations.

C1.justification: The headline accuracy claims and contribution without fine-tuning or a reward model remain intact. V3's introduction broadens applicability to any off-the-shelf pretrained model, explicitly claims preservation of general capabilities, and extends token-efficiency claims to R1-distilled models. These extend the retained contribution without redefining the central method.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations of non-STEM generalization, human preferences, and scaling with model size in Appendix A.2. It expands the favorable step-length range from 200–400 to 200–500 despite unchanged plotted curves. It also removes the explicit instruction-following caveat about math-specialized models and reframes limitations around general inference overhead and broader applicability.

D1.justification: V3 adds a brief L2M implementation description and human annotation instructions. The explicit explanation that eight V100s could not accommodate Qwen2-72B SGR in float32 disappears from Limitations, although hardware and precision choices remain documented. Existing SGR prompts and hyperparameters are retained, with no new code or data release.

R1.justification: V3 adds references for L2M, DROP, SimpleQA, and self-consistency, while removing Kojima et al. (2022), Parthasarathy et al. (2024), and Renze and Guven (2024). The central relationships to SBP, BoN, and RAG persist; shortened reference author lists are bibliographic presentation changes.

P1.justification: The introduction, experimental-results narrative, and limitations undergo substantial rewriting. Guidance and Answer become nested subsections, Self-Reflection receives a separate subsection, and the appendix gains a comparison narrative and reorganized example headings. Terminology, author information, and the recurring 'Guidied' spelling are also revised.

P2.justification: V3 substantially reorganizes the displays: main Table 1 is abridged, its full comparisons become appendix Tables 5–6, and highlighting conventions change. Table 4 and the human preference Figure 5 are added. Existing figures are relocated or relabeled without changing their curves. The new appendix table captions incorrectly exchange the mathematical and MMLU-STEM dataset descriptions.

improvement.justification: V3 modestly strengthens the evidence through a relevant L2M comparison, a test of transfer to DROP, and human judgments showing both an advantage over SBP and a disadvantage to QwQ. These gains outweigh localized reporting problems. However, incomplete new-task protocols, unsupported statistical-significance reporting, overgeneralized summaries in Appendix A.2, and swapped table captions limit the improvement. The central method and original benchmark evidence remain stable.
